title: LangGraph for Fraud Detection: Guardrails, Evals and Langfuse
summary: Joseph Fluckiger replaces a single giant fraud-detection prompt with a LangGraph graph of code and LLM steps.

chapters.title: One Big Prompt vs a Graph
The Graph as a Mermaid Chart

learn: The old agent was a roughly 2,000-line prompt plus about 30 tools; results were non-deterministic and could take 4 minutes.
LangGraph lets him run a directed acyclic graph that mixes deterministic JavaScript functions with LLM nodes, which he says cut runs to 10 to 20 seconds, exportable as a Mermaid chart.
A human approves the agent's findings before anything changes on an account, and labeled simulated data feeds evals per workflow so he can see changes over time.
Langfuse gives visibility into where time goes after his own tracing kept crashing; he calls LangSmith another good option that tends to be cloud-first.
He argues LangGraph suits enterprises because of its guardrails, where a local agent that can do anything on disk carries too much risk.
